'''QT-KT''', also referred to as '''Qutee''', was an [[R-series/Legends|R-series]] [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] member of [[D-Squad/Legends|D-Squad]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. It belonged to [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]].

{{Droid-stub}}

==Biography==
Around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], QT-KT and the rest of D-Squad, led by [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Meebur Gascon/Legends|Meebur Gascon]], were given the mission of infiltrating a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] ship and stealing an encryption module.

When the squad saw the [[Parwan/Legends|Parwan]] doctor [[Gubacher/Legends|Gubacher]], he installed in QT-KT a modification that allowed her to release a high-power [[Magnet/Legends|magnet]]. This came to use during the mission when the squad had to remove several [[Swarm mine/Legends|swarm mines]] from a room. QT's magnet collected the mines and stored them within herself. She soon used them in combat against the droid security squad that discovered their subterfuge. Once [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] managed to snag the module, D-Squad had to escape as the alarm was being sounded. However, Artoo insisted that they not leave [[M5-BZ/Legends|M5-BZ]] behind. Acknowledging that Artoo was right, Gascon said they would repair him on the shuttle. Artoo and QT then helped move BZ to the shuttle, as D-Squad escaped the dreadnaught without alerting suspicion.

==Behind the scenes==
QT-KT was created as a stand-in for [[R2-KT/Legends|R2-KT]], who did not appear in the arc because the ''Clone Wars'' crew wanted to avoid “R2” naming confusion with [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]].<ref name="SW-Clone Wars Download: The Droids You're Looking For">{{SW|url=video/the-droids-you-re-looking-for|series=Clone Wars Download|text=The Droids You're Looking For}} “&hellip;because there's only one 'R2'.”</ref>

In the blog series ''[[From World War to Star Wars]]'', QT-KT alongside the character she was derived from R2-KT's pink coloring as well as acting as a secret weapon was acknowledged as having a precedent during World War II where certain fighter planes, such as one of the Spitfire planes, were colored pink to effectively camouflage them during dawn and dusk to photograph enemy targets without being detected, which had been proposed by Lord Mountbatten for the British Royal Navy.<ref name="From World War to Star Wars">{{SW|url=news/from-world-war-to-star-wars-pink-secret-weapons|text=From World War to ''Star Wars'': Pink Secret Weapons|nolive=1}}</ref>
